Task A independent source review — 2026-10-21
Reviewer: ui_v2_knowledge_backend_review (fresh independent reviewer)

SPEC COMPLIANCE VERDICT: NEEDS CHANGES
CODE QUALITY VERDICT: NEEDS CHANGES
Important findings: 2 (P2); no P0/P1 finding identified in this scoped review.

Scope and authority
Reviewed the current knowledge backend sources, V5__knowledge_authoring_review.sql, KnowledgeAuthoringIntegrationTest, RichDocumentTest, KnowledgeIntegrationTest, KnowledgeDoclingIntegrationTest, and directly relevant UserAdminService permission locking. Compared against contract.txt Task A, task-a-report.txt, UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md knowledge requirements, and progress.txt rulings. The explicit ruling preserving ADMIN-or-KB_EDITOR content editing plus current space ACL supersedes the older category-role wording; independent approval still requires explicit KB_EDITOR and a different author. No HEAD exists: this is a current-source/contract review, not a commit-diff review. No source implementation, Git, database, dependency, Maven/npm/Docker, or browser mutation was performed; only this requested review report was written.

FINDING A1 — P2: Historical source deduplication makes a reverted draft impossible to submit for review
Location: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/knowledge/KnowledgeService.java:142-144; related current-version gate :188 and :202; db/migration/V5__knowledge_authoring_review.sql:40-43.
Reproduction path (deterministic source trace; not executed by reviewer): create an article with fixed title/category and content A, commit it as v1 and let parsing finish without reviewing it. Save content B and commit v2. Then save the same title/category and content A again and commit using a fresh Idempotency-Key. persistUpload searches every non-REJECTED version and returns v1 from the early return. It does not reach the latest_version_id update at line 154, so latest_version_id remains v2. Requesting review for the successful commit result v1 returns 409 VERSION_NOT_READY because v1 is not latest. If v1 was already PENDING when v2 was created, the analogous review endpoint rejects it as non-current. Repeated commits of A continue to return v1. The same mismatch affects file-version reversion.
Actual consequence: a normal undo/revert workflow reports a successful committed upload but cannot proceed through the mandatory current-version review workflow. The UI flags likewise leave v1 without the required review action. An editor must change the content/metadata artificially to escape the dead end.
Suggested fix: reconcile snapshot deduplication with the current-version invariant. Reusing a historical DRAFT/PENDING snapshot must either atomically make that snapshot the current editable version under the existing locks, or create a new eligible revision with appropriately revised uniqueness rules. Keep exact current-version duplicate uploads/idempotent replays deduplicated, retain immutable source and existing publication, and add an A -> B -> A regression proving that the returned version can proceed through independent review/publication. A query-only change to deduplicate latest versions is insufficient unless the cross-history unique indexes are also reconciled.

FINDING A2 — P2: Inline code is escaped as prose before serialization, changing the source text
Location: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/knowledge/RichDocument.java:89-91.
Reproduction path (deterministic source trace; not executed by reviewer): submit a valid RichDoc paragraph containing text "a < b && x_y" with a code mark, then commit it. renderText first calls escape(), giving "a < b && x\_y", and then places that escaped value inside a Markdown code span. The serialized source becomes ` a < b && x\_y `. Markdown code spans retain these entities/backslashes literally; they do not apply prose entity or backslash decoding. Windows paths and punctuation such as asterisks have the same corruption. With multiple permitted marks, previously added Markdown emphasis delimiters can also become literal code contents depending on mark order.
Actual consequence: the immutable RichDoc reader displays the intended command/expression, while the generated private Markdown sent through Docling and onward to chunks/RAG contains changed code. This violates the required source-format fidelity and can give users incorrect copyable instructions or AI answers even though the rich snapshot/hash checks succeed. Existing RichDocumentTest covers escaped prose and links, but no inline-code source fidelity test.
Suggested fix: serialize code spans from the raw normalized text with a delimiter/padding strategy valid for embedded backticks; apply any compatible outer marks outside the code span in a canonical order, or normalize unsupported combinations explicitly. Do not run prose HTML/backslash escaping inside code spans. Add focused cases for <, &, _, *, backslashes, embedded backticks, and combined marks, plus a generated-article parser/source round-trip assertion where supported. Maintain the closed safe RichDoc schema and no executable HTML rendering.

Verified strengths from source and supplied evidence
- Space serialization plus document locks and optimistic draft versions avoid concurrent save overwrites; missing file drafts are read without a GET mutation and require version 0 on first PUT.
- Current active role checks use the same advisory lock as role changes/deactivation; space membership is re-read after the space lock. Independent approval checks explicit current KB_EDITOR, current space edit rights, and reviewer != immutable created_by.
- Review/publish gates reject unapproved and rejected sources. Public detail, versions, chunks and rich content restrict ordinary readers to the current READY/APPROVED published source. Existing publication title/category/pointer remain unchanged during draft and ingest work.
- V5 grandfathering preserves existing publication without invented reviewer IDs; rich source, title/category snapshot, author, SHA and storage key are protected against mutation. Markdown SHA derives from actual generated bytes and generated upload uses the configured storage maximum.
- Mutations and metadata-only audit records share transactions; upload rollback cleanup is registered and has an existing integration check. Replay paths reauthorize access.
- Tree depth/cycle/cross-space/nonempty guards run under the space lock; category subtree filtering retains paging/query behavior.

Evidence inspected (not rerun)

Those logs do not cover A1 or A2, so existing green results do not resolve these findings. No new runtime result is claimed by this review.

Task B independent scoped spec and quality review
Reviewed: 2026-10-21; source-only review, no Git writes, test/build execution, Docker, or database mutation.
Verdict: APPROVE WITH MINOR FOLLOW-UPS for the reviewed Task B implementation. No actionable Critical or Important defect found. This is a source-review verdict, not final integrated-release approval; the latest eleven-test workspace run and broader checks remain root-owned.

Scope and basis
- Read contract.txt Task B/global constraints, task-b-report.txt, progress.txt, workspace controllers/DTO/service, V6 migration, AI cancellation service/controller and worker fencing, ticket unassigned repository/controller, and WorkspaceIntegrationTest.
- Read direct ACL/locking callers in AiAuthorization, CatalogService, UserAdminService, KnowledgeService/Repository and the relevant V3/V4 schema. Compared the worker change with the retained task-b-snapshot; no usable HEAD baseline was invented.
- Evidence inspected: backend-first-green.log lines 157/161/164 reports WorkspaceIntegrationTest 10 and integrated 38 tests, all passing. task-b-review-red.log lines 81/95/98 records one expected assertion failure before the APPROVED predicate adjustment. These are earlier run artifacts, not tests executed by this reviewer. Current eleven-test GREEN was still pending in the reviewed report.

Critical / Important findings
None found in the scoped change.

Minor findings / nonblocking follow-ups
M1. backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/workspace/WorkspaceService.java:93-96
The date parser accepts extended ISO years beyond the advertised YYYY-MM-DD shape and beyond PostgreSQL timestamptz's supported range. A manually supplied narrow range such as from=%2B999999998-01-01&to=%2B999999998-01-01 passes Java parsing and the 366-day check, then reaches SQL parameter binding. Bound dates to the supported four-digit business-date format before querying, returning INVALID_ANALYTICS_RANGE/400. Impact is malformed manual analytics requests failing at the database layer; normal UI dates are unaffected. This is inferred from the parsing/binding path, not runtime reproduced here.
M2. backend/src/test/java/com/ticknova/workspace/WorkspaceIntegrationTest.java:130-135
The in-flight cancellation test covers the successful provider-return branch, but not a retryable provider exception after cancellation or cancellation immediately around expired-lease re-claim. The implementation uses the same event token/lease predicate in complete() and fail(), and the existing AiIntegrationTest contains stale-lease and finite-retry tests, so this is a regression coverage opportunity rather than an observed product bug. Add focused cases when root runs the relevant serialized suite, asserting CANCELLED survives and no retry/success/failure audit is appended by the stale owner.

Positive checks and reasoning
- Portal knowledge matching/snippets/views operate on a MATERIALIZED active reader + can_read + active space + current document/version PUBLISHED + READY + APPROVED set. Popular fallback is deterministic. Categories use the same readable-space boundary. ADMIN alone grants no portal knowledge or ticket content access.
- Ticket portal scope matches existing REQUESTER/AGENT-own and AGENT active queue membership rules. The unassigned filter adds assignee_id IS NULL to both list and total SQL; the original overload/default behavior remains, and combining an assignee with unassigned appropriately yields none.
- View mutation locks the actor and space before current publication authorization and document/version locks. This coordinates with the knowledge membership/publication writers. The database primary key enforces one document/user/UTC-date increment; client counts are not accepted.
- Analytics re-resolves current roles and requires ADMIN, returns only enum/count/date data, uses inclusive UTC date bounds via an exclusive next-day upper bound, enforces a maximum 366-day window, and zero-fills daily values. Ticket status/priority counts use the created-date cohort; resolved counts use actual transitions per day. Published/pending knowledge values are current snapshots. AI completion/refusal/feedback values derive from persisted suggestions/audit events. These semantics are consistent with the report; UI unit/range labels remain outside this review.
- Cancel resolves the creator-owned AI request and current actor, obtains the outbox lock before scope/user/space/ticket checks and job lock, and updates event/job/audit atomically. Other creators cannot target the job. COMPLETED yields 409 and CANCELLED repeats return without duplicate audit. FAILED-to-CANCELLED is currently allowed; the supplied contract specifies 409 for completed results only, so this is not treated as a defect.
- Cancellation, worker claim, complete, and fail all serialize on the event. Once cancellation clears its lease and delivers it, a stale completion/failure cannot pass owns(). If completion wins, cancellation sees COMPLETED after waiting and does not erase the result. Claim recognizes CANCELLED and retains the existing finite retry budget. No new event/job lock inversion was found in these paths.
- V6 adds CANCELLED without removing prior status values; its unique document/user/day key and foreign keys fit the current schema. No model output or ticket mutation is introduced by cancellation.

Declined to judge / limits
- Latest post-APPROVED eleven-test execution, full backend regression, real lock-contention/deadlock/load behavior, fresh/upgrade migration execution, and demo migration: intentionally not run by this reviewer; root owns serialized execution. Source reasoning is not a concurrency stress result.
- Production readiness, real-model/provider behavior, deployability, and performance at production data scale: no corresponding evidence was obtained; mocked integration paths must not be described as real-model validation.
- Frontend UX/accessibility, portal fallback labeling, analytics unit labels, Task A immutable rich snapshots, broader knowledge authoring/review implementation, and root integrations: outside the delegated scope; only direct authorization/schema callers were read.
- General pre-existing AI authorization/RAG hardening is not part of this cancellation-only change. No claim is made that the broader pre-existing subsystem has been exhaustively audited.

F1 [P2] Fence commit before awaiting its prerequisite save.
Location: frontend/src/views/ArticleEditorView.vue:42-46 (especially 44-45).
commit() captures generation/id only after await save(). If the user starts generating a version for article A, confirms navigation to article B (or replaces the session), B loads, and A's old save settles late despite abort, autosave correctly discards A's response but the commit continuation reads the now-current clean B draft and POSTs /B/draft/versions with the new session. The generation check then uses B's generation, so it cannot reject this unintended write/navigation. The same route is reused, so its old async closure remains alive.
Fix: capture document/session/generation and claim the committing guard before the first await; after every await, verify that identity is still current, including save success. Use the original controller/id for the operation, and only clear busy state for that generation.
Regression: deferred PUT that ignores abort; trigger commit on A; navigate/confirm to B or replace session; resolve A after B loads; assert zero commit POSTs and no redirected navigation. Also cover duplicate clicks during the pre-commit save.

F2 [P2] Do not apply the article authoring size cap to an uploaded-file reader.
Location: frontend/src/knowledge/rich.ts:48-49; frontend/src/views/KnowledgeView.vue:43; frontend/src/components/RichDocument.vue:16.
chunksRichDoc normalizes all file chunks as one RichDoc, enforcing the 100000-text-character/1MiB article authoring limits. Existing file ingestion legitimately accepts parser output up to 4MiB (KnowledgeChunker.java:15), and chunks endpoint returns all authorized chunks. A valid file with >100000 displayed characters therefore throws while readerContent/outline/render evaluate. This is outside chunkRead.run's catch and prevents the source from being read, with no actionable load error. Repeated heading paths and chunk overlap can hit the cap even earlier.
Fix: keep closed-schema safety but separate reader limits/representation from authoring limits, or render/paginate safe file chunks directly. Handle conversion/render failure through a visible state rather than an uncaught computed exception. Ensure RichDocument does not reapply the authoring cap to a larger safe file document.
Regression: successful authorized file version with >100000 characters and null rich snapshot remains readable (including source section) without console/render errors. Article authoring limits must remain enforced.

F3 [P2] Purge and fence the category subtree on access denial.
Location: frontend/src/views/KnowledgeView.vue:182-190 and 207; frontend/src/components/KnowledgeCategories.vue:8-23.
The central 403/404 handler clears list/detail/chunks/member state but leaves selectedSpace.canRead and the mounted KnowledgeCategories instance intact. Its rows, selected category name/parent form and independent request generation are outside the operations list. Consequently, revoking space read access and receiving 403/404 from document/list refresh leaves previously authorized category metadata visible; a pending category GET may also populate after the denial. The child's own fail() clears rows but leaves a selected edit form populated, because canEdit remains cached true in the parent. This misses the explicit fresh-denial purge contract already implemented for other server-derived knowledge data.
Fix: invalidate/unmount the category child on denial (until explicit authorized refresh), or pass a shared access epoch/denial state that cancels its requests and clears rows plus server-derived selection/form. Keep user-created unrelated upload inputs as intended.
Regression: populate categories/select edit form; make list/detail/category mutation return 403/404; assert category names/form source values disappear. Resolve a pre-denial category read afterward and assert they stay absent.

F4 [P2] Reset heading indexes for every RichDocument render.
Location: frontend/src/components/RichDocument.vue:5-16.
heading lives in the cached computed closure, outside the component render. The computed getter itself does not read props.content; the returned render function does. When content is replaced while the component stays mounted, rendering increments the old heading counter instead of restarting at zero. richHeadings always builds article-heading-0..N, so TOC links stop matching the DOM after the first rerender. A normal trigger is opening article preview during an in-flight autosave: the saved response replaces content with a fresh object and rerenders the preview.
Fix: create/reset the heading counter inside each complete render traversal (or build a pure render tree with indexes derived from the document).
Regression: mount RichDocument with headings, replace content with an equivalent/fresh document and then changed headings, assert DOM IDs remain aligned with richHeadings after every update; cover preview before autosave response.

Trigger: while initial ticket loading or a filter query is pending, click an enabled inbox tab or Reset (or navigate to another ticket query).

I4 — Important — Reply/notes typed during a successful send are silently erased
Locations: frontend/src/views/TicketDetailView.vue:83-86 and #comment-body textarea in the reply form.
Trigger: send draft A over a slow connection, then continue typing or replace the text with draft B before the comments POST succeeds. The textarea remains editable while mutation.pending is true.
Evidence: sendComment captures the original body, but the success callback unconditionally assigns drafts[kind] = ''.
Consequence: only A reaches the server; B is lost and the new unsaved-change guard sees an empty draft, so it cannot protect this input.
Fix: either disable editing for the submitted destination until the operation completes or clear only when its current value still equals the captured original input. Preserve modifications made after submission. Regression: deferred POST, edit while pending, resolve success, assert the newer text remains (cover public reply and internal note).

I5 — Important — Explicit logout bypasses all new unsaved-change protection
Locations: frontend/src/App.vue:25; frontend/src/stores/session.ts:12; frontend/src/views/NewTicketView.vue:14-15; frontend/src/views/TicketDetailView.vue:23,76; frontend/src/composables/unsaved.ts:5-20.
Trigger: create an unsaved ticket/reply or edit a dirty admin dialog, then click the topbar “退出”.
Evidence: App calls session.logout before navigating. Logout clears the session in finally. Dirty predicates require session.authenticated, and new-ticket/detail token watchers also erase draft content synchronously. The later router leave guard therefore sees false/empty state.
Consequence: intentional logout discards user input without the promised leave confirmation, even though ordinary route navigation is protected.
Fix: have explicit logout consult the registered dirty guard before sending logout/clearing session, while retaining immediate security cleanup for actual expiry/401. Avoid clearing then asking permission. Regression: dirty draft + logout + cancel retains session/content and sends no logout; confirm then logs out; expired-session path still leaves without blocking.

I6 — Important spec gap — Detail tablet side panels are stacked blocks, not the contracted drawers
Locations: frontend/src/views/TicketDetailView.vue:117 onwards; frontend/src/styles.css:488-489; .work/ui-v2/contract.txt Task D.

Both detail panels are always rendered as inline aside blocks with v-show; at <=850px CSS changes the full detail grid to a vertical flex column.
